newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures fell after hopes for further interest rate cuts in Germany were dampened by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing.
The December bond future followed the Bund contract lower before finding support around 126.40 after Issing said on German television he saw no reason for further cuts in key German interest rates.
Traders said, however, French bonds remained reasonably well supported by domestic demand and that the contract would also find support at the gap left between 126.12 and 126.16.
One said the contract could well remain stuck in a zone of consolidation between 126.16 and 126.70 right through to the end of the week given the lack of market-moving economic statistics.

Another trader at a French brokerage said U.S. economic figures, especially the September jobs report, due for release next week were the main focus for bonds. "There's not much until then. We're waiting with impatience."

Although few were expecting the Bundesbank to ease its repo rate after its policy council meeting on Thursday, interest rate futures for next year suffered in both France and Germany after the Issing comments.
December 1996 PIBOR fell one basis point but September and December 1997 contracts both fell five basis points.
Still the PIBOR back months outperformed Euromarks with the spread between the December 1997 contracts narrowing to seven basis points. The spread was negative for contracts further out.

The relatively good performance of the franc helped PIBOR contracts resist the worst of the sell off. The franc suffered early in the session, hitting a low of 3.3842 per mark but rallied to trade at 3.3793 late on Wednesday.
The outperformance at the short end in France also brought the five-year spread into parity.
The 10-year area of the French curve also outperformed with the spread between the 6.50 percent October 2006 OAT and the April 2006 Bund moving to minus four basis points from minus two.
